data.name: Mihraz
data.gender_notes: Mihraz is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Islamic architecture, the Mihrab is a niche in the wall of a mosque indicating the direction of the Kaaba in Mecca. The person who ensures the Mihrab is clean and well-maintained is known as Mihraz. The name Mihraz carries the meaning “Guardian of the Mihrab” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Mihraz usually hope their child will grow to embody guardian of the mihrab and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A guardian of spiritual direction and guidance.
data.etymology: Mihraz belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Guardian of the Mihrab.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Mihraz total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

in_english.name: Mihraz
in_english.long_meaning: In Islamic architecture, the Mihrab is a niche in the wall of a mosque indicating the direction of the Kaaba in Mecca. The person who ensures the Mihrab is clean and well-maintained is known as Mihraz.

data.cultural_impact: The Mihrab, as a physical structure, marks and symbolizes the unity of Muslims towards the holiest site in Islam, the Kaaba in Mecca. It denotes the common direction of the Muslim community in prayers towards Mecca, emphasizing their shared faith and spiritual connection.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Mihraz holds deep spiritual significance as it represents the spiritual anchor guiding Muslims to the House of Allah (Kaaba). It underlines the importance of unwavering faith, commitment and unity with fellow believers, enabling each one to focus their prayers towards Allah and seek His blessings.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Ibn Sa'd, Kitab Al-Tabaqat Al-Kabir, Volume 2, Page 165. The name Mihraz carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Mihraz was the name of a building in Mecca where the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) used to perform the Tawaf (pilgrimage around the Kaaba) before the construction of the Masjid al-Haram (Great Mosque) in Mecca.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Al-Baladhuri, Ansab Al-Ashraf, Volume 1, Page 377. The name Mihraz carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Mihraz was also the name of a structure in the Prophet's Mosque in Medina, where the Imam led the congregational prayers. It was located near the Prophet's pulpit and was used as a place for the Imam to ascend the pulpit (minbar) during his sermons.

modern_usage.modern_context: The term 'Mihraz' originates from Islamic architecture and refers to a niche or recess in a mosque that marks the direction of Mecca. In modern contexts, the term has expanded beyond architecture and is used in various fields. In Interior Design, Mihraz is used as a design element to create a prayer space at home. Middle Eastern Architecture Websites showcase beautiful examples of Mihraz designs from various mosques around the world. Virtual Reality Apps allow users to explore and experience the intricacies of Mihraz designs in a 360-degree view, providing a new way to appreciate this important aspect of Islamic architecture.

name_in_real_life.story: A successful entrepreneur named Ibrahim Mihraz in Cairo, Egypt attributes much of their success to the blessing of their name Mihraz, which means "Guardian of the Mihrab". They believe their name has shaped their identity and guided them through life.
